svg.title: The smoothing index stays fixed or increases by one at each forward step. Thus, if j = J(i + 1) and u = J(i), then u = j or u = j −1. Requiring L = block(i) ≥EP (j) gives B(j, u)2 ≤L and L ≥2/w(j). The one-step price B(j, u)/L is at most L−1/2. Moreover 2w(u) ≤2 ≤Lw(j). These give contraction and width crossing with θ = 1/2. The same adjacency ensures that w(u) is no greater than either analytic width required at the crossing. All thresholds depend on the previously chosen prices, rather than on the subsequently chosen L. For the age bound, put Z(k) = 3 + log bβk, where bβk > 1, and let s > 0 be the coupling slope.
